question.problem: If ${X}_{1}∼N(-2,1)$ and ${X}_{2}∼N(-3,10)$ are independent, then what is the distribution of $Y=3{X}_{1}+2{X}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
Y=a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}Y=3{X}_{1}+2{X}_{2} & ∼N(3\cdot (-2)+2\cdot (-3),{3}^{2}\cdot 1+{2}^{2}\cdot 10) \\  & ∼N(-12,49).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y∼N(-12,49).$
